children: agreed to acquire Calytrix Bio for up to $1.5 billion in cash. The total includes an upfront payment and further payments tied to clinical and regulatory milestones. Lilly shares rose 0.94% as of 11:00 a.m. ET.

Calytrix's lead program is a preclinical antibody that targets mutant calreticulin, a genetic alteration behind essential thrombocythemia and myelofibrosis. Both are rare disorders that cause the bone marrow to produce too many abnormal blood cells. The antibody is designed to hit both main types of the mutation, depleting the cells that drive the disease while sparing healthy blood production. Current treatments manage symptoms rather than target those cells. Calytrix CEO Brad Prosek said patients deserve therapies that do more than manage symptoms.
The deal adds to Lilly's blood cancer business, which already includes the approved drug Jaypirca, and follows its $2.3 billion purchase of Ajax Therapeutics earlier this year.

title: Lilly Bets Up to $1.5 Billion on Calytrix's Preclinical Antibody
